newsitem.title: USA: Goldman sees Canada dlr rally to C$1.33 - report.
newsitem.headline: Goldman sees Canada dlr rally to C$1.33 - report.

text.p: Goldman, Sachs and Co Inc expects the Canadian dollar to start to strengthen, with a move to C$1.33 per U.S. dollar likely by year end, according to its research publication, The Weekly Analyst.
Goldman, Sachs has been "extremely bullish" on Canada's improving economic fundamentals and as a result on the underlying prospects for the Canadian dollar, the report said.
The Canadian dollar traded at C$1.3674/79 per dollar at 1451 EDT/1851 GMT.
To date, Goldman, Sachs' enthusiasm has been tempered by the need for monetary ease and sharply negative Canada-U.S. interest rate differentials, The Weekly Analyst said.

However, the Bank of Canada's (BOC) warning that it may now be "drawing a line in the sand" and the prospective announcement this week of Canada's first quarterly current account surplus in more than a decade should provide momentum for a stronger Canadian dollar, the report said.
The Goldman Sachs Dynamic Equilibrium Exchange Rate (GSDEER) valuation levels for the dollar stand at C$1.32 on an unadjusted basis and C$1.15 on an adjusted basis, it said.
"We continue to look for an appreciation to C$1.33 by year's end," said the Goldman, Sachs research report.
Thus Goldman, Sachs recommended establishing long Canadian dollar spot positions against the U.S. dollar but shorting Canadian Treasury bill or BAX positions, the report said.
At the same time, the Wall Street firm suggested setting stop loss buy orders above C$1.3850, the report said.

"Monetary conditions have been relaxed considerably in 1996 and we expect a partial reversing by year end, with a stronger (Canadian dollar) and higher interest rates," according to the report. -- N.A. Treasury Desk 212-859-1668
